  <max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>0.4</max_server_memory_usage_to_ram_ratio>

data.mycel-users.xml:
<!-- GENERATED by `mycel cluster generate` from the cluster mycelfile — do not edit by hand. -->
<clickhouse>
  <users>
    <!-- The built-in admin, used only inside this container: the health probe and the
         system-log cleanup. Loopback only (replace drops the image's own ::/0 for it), and
         its password comes from the container's environment, never from this file. -->
    <default>
      <password from_env="MYCEL_CLICKHOUSE_ADMIN_PASSWORD"/>
      <networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks>
    </default>

    <!-- The kpi module's write identity. It owns this database's DDL — the module creates
         mycel_kpi and its event table at boot — so it needs CREATE/ALTER, not only INSERT.
         No other module in the cluster is given a ClickHouse credential at all. Any address:
         the pod network is not known here, so the boundary is the NetworkPolicy (only the
         kpi module may reach port 9000) and the per-environment password. -->
    <kpi_writer>
      <password from_env="MYCEL_CLICKHOUSE_WRITER_PASSWORD"/>
      <networks><ip>::/0</ip></networks>
      <profile>default</profile>
      <quota>default</quota>
      <grants>
        <query>GRANT CREATE DATABASE, CREATE TABLE, ALTER, INSERT, SELECT ON mycel_kpi.*</query>
      </grants>
    </kpi_writer>

    <!-- Read-only. Grafana's datasource AND the module's own rollup read through this,
         so the query path physically cannot write. Its password, like the others, comes
         from the container's environment. -->
    <kpi_reader>
      <password from_env="MYCEL_CLICKHOUSE_READER_PASSWORD"/>
      <networks><ip>::/0</ip></networks>
      <profile>default</profile>
      <quota>default</quota>
      <grants>
        <query>GRANT SELECT ON mycel_kpi.*</query>
      </grants>
    </kpi_reader>
  </users>
</clickhouse>
